senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. רעד) [to vibrate,] to thunder, rumble, roar.

units: <cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 33:2">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXXIII</cite> ed. Schechter <he>מצרים הִרְעִימוּ עליהם בקולם אף הקב״ה ה׳ עליהם קולו</he> the Egyptians roared at (threatened) them with their voices, so did the Lord cause his voice to roar at them (<cite ref="II Samuel 22:14">II Sam. XXII, 14</cite>); (oth. ed. <he>ה׳ עליהם בקול על הים</he>, ref. to <cite ref="Job 37:5">Job XXXVII, 5</cite>). Midr. Sam. ch. V <he>אם עולים … אני מַרְעִים בקולי וכ׳</he> if they rise up to heaven, from there I will thunder with my voice and throw them down; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 86:3">Yalk. Sam. 86</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to cause to murmur. Ib. 77 (ref. to הרעמה, I Sam. I, 6) את מַרְעֶמֶת אותה וכ׳ thou makest her ‘thunder’ against me, … there are no thunders which are not followed by (fructifying) rain, I will visit her at once; Pesik. R. s. 43 מְתַרְעֶמֶת (fr. תִּרְעֵם).
units: <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 43:1">Ib.</cite> <he>בעבור הַרְעִימָהּ על אלהים לטובתה</he> in order to make her murmur against God (complain in prayer) for her own good.

senses.gloss: (v. תַּרְעוּמֶת) to be excited, rebel, be discontented.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 6a:6">Meg. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>זבולון מִתְרַעֵם על מדותיו היה</he> Zebulun was dissatisfied with the measures he received (the share of the land allotted to him).

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 11:1">Pesik. R. s. 11</cite> <he>כולם מִתְרַעֲמִים ומרגישים</he> all the nuts in the pile are disturbed and in commotion; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 992:10">Yalk. Cant. 992</cite>.
